**STEP 1 - Scene:** This is a single slice of white or sourdough-style bread, lightly toasted, on an otherwise empty plate.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** It is a large square white dinner plate, about 26 cm across. Its area is roughly 26 × 26 ≈ 676 cm² for a square, or about 600 cm² of usable area allowing for the rounded rim.

**STEP 3 - Items:** One slice of bread, crust on, lightly toasted. There is no visible butter or spread, only a few crumbs.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The slice measures about 13 × 14 cm and is slightly irregular, so about 160 cm². That is about 25% of the plate area, and nothing else covers the plate.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** 160 cm² × 1.2 cm thick ≈ 190 ml gross volume.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** I did not use the suggested 0.9–1.0 g/ml for bread-like slices. This bread has large holes, and at that density the slice would weigh about 180 g, which is unrealistic. I used about 0.3 g/ml instead, which matches the bread-loaf figure. That gives 190 × 0.3 ≈ 57 g, rounded to about 55 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Lightly toasted white or sourdough bread has about 270 kcal per 100 g. So 55 g × 2.7 ≈ 149 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A large sourdough slice typically weighs 45–65 g and provides 120–170 kcal, so the estimate is plausible.
